newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: French fight off mortar attack in Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: French fight off mortar attack in Central Africa.

text.p: French troops fought gunbattles with local army mutineers in Central African Republic on Thursday but France said its men acted in self-defence and would not be embroiled in the worsening conflict.

French soldiers helping government forces contain the uprising, which has paralysed the capital Bangui since November 16, fired back as mutineers trying to break out of their strongholds rained mortar shells on the city centre.
Witnesses said the fighting claimed the lives of at least two rebels.
Shells landed around the French-owned Sofitel hotel and gunfire fire ripped through two hotel rooms, a manager said.
An official defence ministry source in Paris said the French soldiers had fired back in "legitimate self-defence" when the rebels fired four rocket-propelled grenades at the hotel.

"Clashes took place between 2.30 and 6.00 a.m. between the mutineers and loyalist forces. The Sofitel was targeted. Four RPGs were fired at the hotel. It seems two hit the hotel without causing casualties," the source said.
French forces came under attack while they were evacuating the hotel and returned fire in self-defence, after which calm was restored, he said.

"The situation in Bangui is difficult because at this moment a number of mutineers and rebels are threatening the balance of the country, but there is no question of French troops entering an internal conflict," Defence Minister Charles Million said.

He told reporters after meeting his Italian counterpart that the role of the French troops permanently stationed in the strategic country was limited to "participating in maintaining legality and protecting our nationals".
No one was hurt in the hotel attack but guests fled into darkened streets and the nearby bush.
The hotel is close to the French embassy, one of the key sites protected by French troops based in the former colony under bilateral accords.

"There was shooting from both sides, but the rebels were firing only rockets. Two rooms have been hit and shells landed in the hotel yard," front office manager Martin Mbekiyanga told BBC radio's French service.
He said French troops had asked to use the hotel's rooftop to get a better view of rebel positions.
A resident said rebel fire came from the Kassai barracks outside Bangui where rebels control the main armoury there.

"Some presidential guard troops were deployed a few metres from the Hotel Sofitel. French troops were positioned a little further down," the resident said. "Rebels aimed mortar fire at the two groups, who fired back at the rebels."
Witnesses said an estimated 400 rebels joined the attack. There were no details of their report of two rebel deaths.

The mutiny is the third mounted this year by troops complaining about pay and conditions. They have now hardened their demands into a drive to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse and to disarm civilian militias and mercenaries from Chad and Sudan they say are hired by the head of state.

French troops helped Patasse quell a more violent revolt in May in which the capital was looted by mutineers. Although France reinforced its garrison at the start of the current uprising, French troops have largely kept a low profile, restrictiong their role to protection.
They have not confronted rebels who have been disarming civilians in some Bangui districts, triggering an exodus of people from Patasse's tribe from such areas.
